what_happened: Task 608's target (<leader>as chat pane styling) resolves to the sf1 terminal integration, which only toggles a snacks.terminal window around the external vendor binary ~/.sapience/sf1.py. That file is untracked (no git repo), fetched by plain curl from app.spnc.ai, and silently overwritten by a daily auto-update (confirmed in ~/.sapience/update.log). No change confined to /home/benjamin/.config/nvim can durably add message-part dividers; the fix is either a disposable vendor hand-edit, a PTY-proxy wrapper built inside this repo (pattern-matching on sf1's literal output text), or a separate task in ~/.dotfiles/packages/sapience-flake to reapply the patch at each sapience update. Flagged user_decision in .return-meta.json.

The research report's Finding 3 (sf1's output is a strictly append-only line stream; the only cursor repositioning is the transient \r\033[2K indicator on stderr, cleared before any stdout write) was the exact feasibility fact the plan needed, so the pty-filter design could be written without re-deriving it. Only a short re-verification pass against the live sf1.py was needed, not a re-read of all 653 lines.

Planning surfaced a hazard the research report did not name: GNU readline re-emits the sf1 prompt on every line edit (arrow key, backspace), so a naive prompt-pattern match would inject one blank line per keystroke. Required adding an explicit fresh-prompt discrimination rule (prompt counts as fresh only when reached via \n, never \r, with a one-shot latch) as Phase 1's primary unit-test target rather than leaving it to implementation-time discovery.
